sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the statement made in the FIR itself reveals that this is purely a civil suit and for recovery of money the informant can approach the civil forum.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is innocent and no way connected in the alleged offence, only due to some personal grudge, the present criminal case is filed against him.

More so,
the petitioner is behind the bar for 40 days and his further custodial detention is not necessary for the purpose of investigation.

The petitioner is a permanent resident of aforesaid locality and hence,
there is no chance of absconding, if he is enlarged on bail.

In this context learned APP has submitted that sufficient incriminating materials is found in the case diary against the petitioner and from the statement made by the accused himself and from the statement of other witnesses also, it is seen that after taking the car from the informant on rent he also took Rs. 65,000/- for repairing the body of the said car and thereafter, the car has been sold out to some other person in connivance with other co-accused persons.

The investigation is still under progress and till date, the vehicle could not be recovered and accordingly, it is submitted that further custodial interrogation may be necessary for the just and proper investigation of the case.

After hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both sides, I have also perused the case dairy, from which it reveals that sufficient incriminating materials have already collected by the I.O. against the petitioner.
Hence, I find that further custodial interrogation may be necessary for the purpose of the just Page No.# 3/3 and proper investigation of the case.
Hence, I do not find proper to allow the accused petitioner to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, his bail prayer is rejected.
Bail application stands disposed of.
